chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Habib from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The testimony for the sighting of the crescent is not valid with fewer than fifty men, the number for oaths; and the testimony of two men is valid only if they are from outside the city, and there is an impediment in the city, so they inform that they saw it and inform about a people who fasted for the sighting.

key_terms.عَدَدَ الْقَسَامَةِ: The number for oaths (referring to qasamah)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for accepting the testimony of two men for moon sighting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlighting the juristic distinction between the stringent requirement of fifty witnesses for general lunar sighting and the concession for two witnesses when external impediments prevent broader verification. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on rigorous evidentiary standards while accommodating practical realities in community calendar determination. The hadith underscores the importance of verifying the reliability of witnesses and the conditions under which reduced testimony is legally sufficient for establishing religious months.
